Customize glyvis plots with tidyplots

glyvis_plot_options.Rd

All plot_*() functions and statistical autoplot() methods return a tidyplot, which also inherits from ggplot. Continue styling with tidyplots::adjust_*() functions, add components with tidyplots::add_*(), or use ordinary ggplot2 layers. No global theme or options are changed.

Common options

Pass these named arguments through ... in any plotting entry point:

  • title: optional plot title.

  • width, height: plot-area dimensions in millimetres; NULL (default) uses tidyplots defaults (50 by 50 mm). Set NA to fill the available graphics device. These are not export-page dimensions.

  • fontsize: base text size in points, default 9.

  • family: font family, default "sans".

  • palette: color vector. A named vector maps group names to fixed colors across different plots and subsets. Unnamed palettes follow factor order; use the same factor levels or a named palette for consistent group colors. Continuous heatmaps use blue-white-red; other plots use distinct hues.

Plot-specific options

  • PCA: axes = c(1, 2), label = FALSE, add_ellipse = FALSE, and top_n = NULL for loading arrows. Biplots rescale arrows by a common display multiplier; scores and explained variance are unchanged.

  • PCA, PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, t-SNE, UMAP and volcano scatter plots: point_size = 2 (volcano: 1.5), alpha = 0.8 (volcano: 0.7), and label = FALSE. Embedding score plots also accept add_ellipse = FALSE.

  • Loading plots: label = FALSE, top_n = NULL. All arrows are retained by default. An explicit top_n selects the largest squared loading norms.

  • VIP and ranked dot plots: top_n = NULL; an explicit positive integer selects the largest plotted values. All variables are retained by default.

  • Boxplots: points = TRUE, ncol = NULL, label_width = 24, and scales = "free_y". Long facet labels wrap without truncation. Points are observations; boxes show the median and quartiles with 1.5-IQR whiskers. Use scales = "fixed" for comparisons across facets.

  • Heatmaps: scale = "row" (also "column" or "none"), cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_cols = TRUE (also FALSE or compatible hclust objects), show_rownames = FALSE, show_colnames = NULL, and na_col = "grey90". Columns are labelled automatically up to 40 samples. Values are log2(abundance + 1), then optionally standardized. Clustering orders rows and columns; dendrograms are not drawn inside the heatmap. Use the hierarchical-clustering autoplot() method for a dendrogram.

  • Correlation plots: label = FALSE, digits = 2, and triangle = "lower" (also "upper" or "full"). Colors span -1 to 1.

  • Sequence logos: pass glyph options in logo_args, a named list passed to ggseqlogo::geom_logo(), e.g. list(method = "prob").

Migration from earlier backends

Arguments specific to factoextra, EnhancedVolcano, GGally, pheatmap, and ggdendrogram are no longer forwarded. Unsupported arguments error instead of being ignored. Use the options above or modify the returned tidyplot. Replace PCA geom = "point" with the default label = FALSE, repel = TRUE with label = TRUE, and volcano pointSize with point_size. Move ggseqlogo arguments from ... into logo_args.

Export

Use ggplot2::ggsave() with explicit width, height and units, or tidyplots::save_plot(). PDF/SVG preserve vector elements and editable text; use a suitable graphics device and inspect labels at the final physical size. Large feature sets may require a larger output, label suppression, or an explicitly selected subset. Automatic label repulsion may omit crowded text but never removes the underlying observations.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("glystats", quietly = TRUE)) {
  mat <- matrix(c(3, 8, 5, 9, 2, 7, 6, 4, 1, 5, 6, 2), nrow = 3,
    dimnames = list(paste0("V", 1:3), paste0("S", 1:4)))
  se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(mat))
  p <- plot_pca(se, title = "PCA", fontsize = 9)
  p |> tidyplots::adjust_size(width = 80, height = 60)
}
